subject: Day 14: two weeks old; growth spurt opens; EPDS this week
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 14. Two weeks old, week three opens. The first growth spurt is likely starting: 24-48 hours of unusually frequent feeding, then a reset. If breastfeeding, supply calibrates to this demand — let it.

Action items
- Treat today and tomorrow as feeding-heavy; the spurt is a normal supply calibration, not a problem to fix.
- Complete the EPDS maternal mood screen this week; a score of 13 or higher traditionally distinguishes likely depression and warrants a call. Postpartum Support International: https://www.postpartum.net/
- Open the 529 plan now that the SSN should have arrived. 529 plan overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Verify Avi's health-insurance enrollment processed with the insurer directly. Healthcare.gov on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Continue the feeding and output log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cluster feeding for 24-48 hours, evening fussiness, a stronger need to be held.
- [low concern] Baby acne — neonatal cephalic pustulosis — peaking around three to four weeks and resolving on its own.
- [monitor] Tearfulness or anxiety in Anoushka beyond what the baby's schedule imposes; baby blues should be resolving by now.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight stagnation. Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Accumulate 10-15 minutes of tummy time across awake-alert windows after feeds. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold him at a mirror for 30-60 seconds — the face-tracking response is the point.
- If raising him bilingual, make sure the second-language parent is already speaking that language consistently.
- Respond to his vocalizations in turn-taking exchanges during calm-alert time. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 17-21: growth spurt resolving.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.
- Day 35-42: peak crying curve approaches around six weeks.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
